title: Shadows
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Shadows Worksheets (Opaque, Translucent, Transparent)
standard_text: Recognise that shadows are formed when the light from a light source is blocked by an opaque object. Find patterns in the way that the size of shadows change.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on shadows: how shadows form, opaque, translucent and transparent materials, shadow size and position, and shadows from the Sun. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Closer to the light, bigger shadow.
body_html:
How to think about it

A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light from a light source.

  • Opaque materials block all light; translucent let some through; transparent let almost all through.
  • The shadow falls on the side away from the light and has the same outline as the object.
  • The closer the object is to the light, the bigger the shadow.
Example

Torch on the left of a cup. Shadow?

Opposite side

Answer: on the right

Example

Move the toy nearer the torch. Shadow?

Blocks more light

Answer: bigger

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a shadow is a reflection.
  • Thinking shadows point towards the light.
  • Thinking moving away from the torch makes the shadow bigger.

faq.a: When an opaque object blocks light from a light source, a dark area forms behind it on the side away from the light. That is a shadow.

faq.q: How can you change the size of a shadow?
faq.a: Move the object closer to the light to make the shadow bigger, or further from the light to make it smaller.

faq.q: What is the difference between opaque, translucent and transparent?
faq.a: Opaque materials let no light through and make dark shadows. Translucent materials let some light through. Transparent materials let almost all light through.
